To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
by using a hybrid metasurface, we are able to switch the optical properties of the structure from a high-contrast scattering to a low-contrast scattering and back again, in a reversible way.

we propose an active control on magnetic and electric interference in a hybrid metasurface by employing the thermo-optic effect, and this allows a switchable and reversible control on the optical properties of the metasurface, including the Kerker effect and Fano-like resonances.

by using hybrid metal-dielectrics metasurfaces, it is possible to achieve a switchable sharp Fano resonance with high contrast and tunability in the optical properties, and also a 10-fold enhancement of the intensity of the third harmonic generation, which are of high importance in many applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optical properties of hybrid plasmonic-dielectric nanostructures.

the development of novel types of optical hybrid nanostructures, where the optical properties are controlled by temperature, and consequently, by heating, which is an efficient, reversible, and non-destructive method.
the design and fabrication of hybrid metasur- faces, consisting of gold nanostructures and silicon nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed hybrid metal-dielectrics metasurfaces can be used for controlling the interference among electric and magnetic modes in the system, and consequently the Kerker condition.

the hybrid metasurface proposed in this study is a versatile platform for controlling and switching the optical properties of the metasurface in an active manner, which is of great importance in the design and fabrication of metasurface based devices.

by employing the thermo-optic effect of silicon and metal nanoantennas, we demonstrate an active and reversible control on the interference between electric and the magnetic modes of the hybrid nanostructure and consequently on the Kerker condition and Fano-like resonance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed hybrid metasurafces are a new class of active metasurfaces that can control the scattering and absorption properties of light via thermal tuning.
we propose a new class of hybrid metasurfaes for the first time, and we show that the hybrid nature of this metasurface is the key to the unique and novel optical properties.
we have proposed a hybrid metal-dielectic metasurface, which allows a precise control on the interference between electric and magentic modes and consequently, on the Kerker condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hybrid metasurfaes can be designed for controlling and manipulating light-matter interactions in a highly efficient and versatile manner.

by combining the advantages of metallic and dielectrics nanostructures we can achieve novel optical properties with a wide range of tunability, and therefore, a wide range of possible applications in the fields of optics and photonics.
hybrid metasurfaes, with a combination of metallic and dielectic elements, can provide us with a wide range of tunable optical properties, including switching, nonlinear and slow light effects.
